answer: Locks are written down in trellis, expire in karst, and cipher lists each expiry. The admission bond is time locked for 20 epochs, longer than any single challenge window, so capital cannot be cycled between aliases within one epoch. A hostile operator running 67 aliases as a result needs 28 simultaneously locked bonds rather than one rotating pool. So the marginal impostor costs more than the marginal honest participant earns in 2 epochs. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
